prompt:
Return only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or JSON null. No prose or Markdown.

Use only the note's contact block: recognize variant labels, colon/equals/tab separators, and any line order. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent lines, blanks, and whole-value -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD (any case) are missing. Never guess or derive fields from notes, signatures, domains, or company suffixes.

Reserve the country line for country. Elsewhere route values containing @ to email; route to phone if stripping leading tel: and a trailing numeric extension (ext. N, ext N, xN, #N, extension N) leaves at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . /. Route regardless of label and do not reuse routed values. Use remaining labeled name/company values, swapping before cleanup if the name-line value ends with a legal suffix and the company-line value does not.

Country: normalize the supplied line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English/Swedish/German names, alpha-2/alpha-3 codes, case-insensitively, and common aliases including UK/Great Britain→GB, Holland→NL, USA/U.S.A.→US, Türkiye→TR, Czech Republic→CZ.

Phone: strip tel: and extension. A start of + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis, means international. Remove (0) from international numbers; remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses and convert initial 00 to +. Preserve the international calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. If country is missing and the international code uniquely identifies a country, fill its alpha-2 code; shared codes such as +1 or +7 do not fill country. This is the sole exception to missing fields staying null. For national numbers strip formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the supplied country's calling code; without country, return phone null. Non-null phone is E.164 (+ and digits only).

Name: split Last, First at the first comma and reorder. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof (any case, optional dot). Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and optional preceding comma, trim, and apply the same casing to each space-separated word. For swaps and removal, match suffixes case-insensitively: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; never transliterate. Email: strip mailto: and surrounding angle brackets and lowercase the whole address. Use JSON null, not an empty string, for missing values.
